analysis.title: The Day Ahead - North America, Friday October 23, 2026
key_insights: Nasdaq Composite fell 2.60% to 26,008.86 (the text body prints 25,008.86, the stock table and the 694-point change support 26,008.86), its steepest daily drop since June. The S&P 500 fell 1.21% to 7,663.43 and the Dow rose 0.02% to 52,867.98. Meta and Tesla earnings did little to ease AI-spending concerns.
The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index lost 6.72% to 10,731.98. Lam Research fell 11.61% and Coherent fell 12.68% in the S&P 500 losers list.

Meta fell 6.98% to $648.85 despite better-than-expected results and a strong forecast. It raised the low end of its 2026 capex range by $5 billion to $135-145 billion, plans to sell new stock to help fund it, and posted its first cash burn in more than a decade. Meta's credit default swap cost hit a record, which the report reads as AI cost fears spreading to credit markets.

Tesla fell 3.08% to $374.58 after cutting its 2026 capex forecast to about $20 billion from more than $25 billion. Spending on AI and robotics came in far below plan, producing a surprise positive free cash flow. An analyst quoted says a smaller budget hints at slower growth.

Treasuries rallied on the equity selloff. The 10-year yield was 4.9695% after a 1-11/32 price gain, the 2-year 4.6609% and the 30-year 5.2953%. A Sage Advisory strategist says flight-to-quality is now winning over the energy-driven inflation concern, even though markets had priced in inflation and possible Fed rate increases.

Oil rose after Houthi attacks in Saudi Arabia. Brent futures gained 3.97% to $113.14 and WTI gained 2.21% to $99.36. The Houthis are pushing toward the Bab el-Mandeb chokepoint, and a PVM analyst says attacks on ships in the Strait of Hormuz and on Saudi oil infrastructure outweigh reports of exports above pre-conflict levels.

Spot gold fell 2.78% to $4,025.48 per ounce as higher oil raised inflation worries and expectations that rates stay elevated. Markets look to next week's Fed meeting, and the quoted metals trader expects further Fed hikes. Copper fell 2.8%.

The yen rose, with the dollar down 0.8% to 156.86 yen, on safe-haven demand. A Convera strategist cites an intervention premium as the pair nears 160. The euro fell 0.16% to $1.1214 on French social unrest and fiscal worries, and the dollar index fell 0.14% to 101.63.
Treasury sold $26 billion of 5-year TIPS at a 2.367% high yield with a 2.41 bid-to-cover ratio.

P&G now expects higher raw material, energy and freight costs to cut fiscal 2027 profit by about $1.4 billion, up from $1 billion, with cost pressure rising over the next two quarters. Demand for beauty and home-care products held up.

Delta, Southwest and American lowered 2026 earnings forecasts because airfare increases have not caught up with fuel. Airlines now expect $4.25-4.85 a gallon, up from well below $4.00 in the third quarter.

Valero posted record quarterly profit. Refining margin per barrel nearly tripled to $39.24 and refining adjusted operating earnings rose over 400% to $8.8 billion, driven by supply disruption from the Iran and Ukraine wars.

Union Pacific beat third-quarter profit estimates. Fuel costs hurt its operating ratio by 140 basis points, but the ratio improved 10 basis points to 59.1%. Revenue rose 15%, and freight revenue excluding fuel surcharges rose 6%. Norfolk Southern also beat on adjusted profit. UNP is pursuing an $85 billion deal for Norfolk Southern.

Lockheed Martin agreed to sell the Pentagon at least 850 F-35 jets over 10 years, worth potentially at least $78 billion, and raised its annual sales and profit forecasts above estimates. It will hold production at 156 aircraft a year and self-fund at least $7 billion of F-35 initiatives.
Comcast flagged over $1 billion of fourth-quarter restructuring charges ahead of the mid-2027 NBCUniversal spinoff. It lost 144,000 broadband customers against 116,800 expected by analysts.
Spotify forecast fourth-quarter profit above estimates and shares surged. Management credits AI features such as AI DJ and prompt-based playlists for user growth.

Blackstone's Jon Gray says widening credit spreads on AI-related debt for unleased assets may let lenders command higher yields. The comment reflects investors demanding larger premiums to fund leveraged AI buildout.

Anthropic is the only technology IPO left on the fall calendar. It plans to price in mid-November after making its prospectus public as early as late October, with some investors citing a potential $1.5 trillion valuation. Dates are subject to change.

A strong Democratic showing in the US midterms could hamper the data center buildout as public opposition grows over energy costs and environmental strain. Investors see this as a risk to the AI trade.

US initial jobless claims fell 6,000 to 194,000 for the week ended October 17, against a 200,000 forecast. This is the sixth straight week at or below 200,000 and near a 57-year low. Continuing claims rose 25,000 to 1.728 million. Economists describe a low-hire, low-fire labor market.

Data today: S&P Global flash PMIs for October (manufacturing forecast 55.5 vs 55.9, services 58.0 vs 58.8, composite prior 58.4) and final University of Michigan sentiment (forecast 46.3, unchanged). American Express (consensus EPS about $4.47-4.48) and SLB (consensus EPS about $0.61-0.62) report before the open. Apple's iPhone Duo foldable goes on sale in stores after online orders sold out in minutes.

Canada: TSX fell 0.97% to 35,973.45 with materials down 5.62% on weaker gold and copper. Celestica fell 12.04%. Canada gave Cleveland-Cliffs 15 days to reverse Ontario job cuts or face sanctions including forced divestiture. August retail sales are due, forecast +1.3% m/m.
earnings_insights: Meta Q3 (reported this week): results better than expected with a strong forecast, but capex guidance raised $5 billion at the low end to $135-145 billion, shares -6.98%. Beat magnitude not given in the report.
Tesla Q3 (reported this week): 2026 capex forecast cut to about $20 billion from over $25 billion, surprise positive free cash flow, shares -3.08%.
Procter & Gamble fiscal Q1 (reported): sales driven by resilient beauty and home-care demand, fiscal 2027 cost headwind now about $1.4 billion vs prior $1 billion estimate.
Union Pacific Q3 (reported): profit beat Wall Street estimates, operating ratio 59.1% (improved 10 bp despite a 140 bp fuel hit), operating revenue +15% y/y.
Norfolk Southern Q3 (reported): adjusted profit beat estimates, fuel costs largely recovered through surcharges.
Lockheed Martin Q3 (reported): raised annual sales and profit forecasts above Wall Street estimates.
Valero Q3 (reported): record quarterly profit, beat expectations, refining margin $39.24 per barrel, refining adjusted operating earnings $8.8 billion.
Comcast Q3 (reported): lost 144,000 broadband customers vs 116,800 FactSet estimate and 91,000 a year ago, over $1 billion restructuring charges flagged for Q4.
Spotify (reported): Q4 profit forecast above Wall Street estimates, shares surged.
American Express Q3 (due Oct 23, 07:00 ET): Smart Estimate EPS $4.47, LSEG IBES EPS estimate $4.48, year-ago $4.14, revenue estimate $20,122 million. These are estimates, not results.

SLB Q3 (due Oct 23, 07:00 ET): Smart Estimate EPS $0.62 (LSEG data cited in text as 61 cents), year-ago $0.69, revenue estimate $9,280 million. These are estimates. Focus areas are Middle East operations recovery, margins and digital business growth.
Delta, Southwest and American lowered 2026 earnings forecasts after Q3 results because of jet fuel costs.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Sixth week at or below 200,000 and near 57-year lows. Points to a stable low-hire, low-fire labor market and a modest October job growth pickup.
Poll expects a slight slowdown from September. Release 09:45 ET Oct 23.
Poll expects services to slip. Composite prior 58.4, no poll.
Expected unchanged. Prior readings: conditions 44.7, expectations 47.3, 1-year inflation expectations 4.7%, 5-year 3.5%.

macro_indicators.reading: +0.43% m/m forecast vs +0.70% prior, 4.73% y/y forecast vs 4.47% prior
macro_indicators.interpretation: Monthly pace expected to slow while the annual rate accelerates.
Indexed 5-year auction result, reported alongside the Treasury rally.
Yields fell on a safe-haven bid as equities sold off, after the market had priced inflation and possible Fed rate increases.
Supply disruption fears from Houthi strikes on Saudi Arabia raise inflation concerns and support expectations of higher-for-longer rates.

risk_factors: AI spending returns: investors doubt the payoff from AI capex and fear government restrictions at local, state or federal level.
Data center backlash and a strong Democratic showing in the US midterms could slow the AI buildout.
Oil above $110 Brent from Middle East disruption feeds inflation, raises company costs (P&G, airlines, Union Pacific) and supports a higher-for-longer rate view.
Possible Fed rate hikes, with the Fed meeting next week.
Widening credit spreads on leveraged AI-related debt.
French bond selloff and social unrest spreading to weaker euro zone borrowers.
Possible yen intervention as USD/JPY nears 160.
Soft IPO market, with the Nasdaq CEO flagging a modest softening.
vol_and_positioning: Meta's cost of insuring its debt against default hit an all-time high, a sign AI spending fears are spreading to credit markets.
Investors had already priced inflation and Federal Reserve rate increase prospects, so the Treasury bid reflects changes in risk assets and financial conditions (Sage Advisory).
Traders see an intervention premium in yen near 160 per dollar, per Convera.
geopolitical: Houthi attacks in Saudi Arabia and clashes with a Saudi-led coalition as the Iran-aligned group pushes toward the Bab el-Mandeb chokepoint at the Red Sea's mouth.
Attacks on ships in the Strait of Hormuz and strikes on Saudi oil infrastructure, in the context of a drawn-out war in the Middle East and the US war on Iran.
War in Ukraine, including a Russian missile attack on a Kyiv shopping centre, cited alongside Iran as a driver of fuel supply disruption.
Possible SpaceX-Tesla merger may draw scrutiny in Beijing and a political fight between President Trump and Democrats, given Tesla's China exposure and SpaceX's defense work.
Canada and Turkey signed a strategic partnership as Carney seeks to reduce reliance on the US, with free trade talks starting next month in Ankara.
Canada gave Cleveland-Cliffs 15 days to reverse Ontario steel mill job cuts or face sanctions including forced divestiture of the Stelco plant.
French social unrest and a worsening fiscal outlook weigh on French bonds and the euro.

tension_points.bear_case: Energy-driven inflation and expected Fed rate increases push yields up and gold down, as higher oil reinforces higher-for-longer rate expectations.

tension_points.bull_case: Blackstone's Gray sees widening credit spreads on AI debt as a chance to earn higher yields, and Spotify shares rose on AI features.
tension_points.bear_case: Investors question the return on investment from AI spending, as Meta's record default insurance cost and first cash burn in over a decade show, with political and regulatory risk from data center backlash.
